title: Mexi Beans and Rice
subtitle: with Sweetcorn and Yoghurt
description: Dial up the flavour on rice and beans by adding tomato, herbs and spices. Top with charred corn and a cherry tomato salsa for the full Mexican experience.

steps.text: Cook rice: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, discard the husk and silks from the corn. Halve the corn widthwise, then carefully cut into wedges lengthwise (see Make it yours). Halve the tomatoes. Pick the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the beans.

Char corn: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the corn for 2-3 mins each side until charred. Remove from the pan, reserving the oil. Return the pan to medium-high heat. Add the coriander stems, garlic, cumin and coriander spice blend and half the tomatoes and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant.

Cook Mexi rice and beans: Add the rice to the tomato mixture and stir to coat. Add the beans, 2 tbs tomato paste, 1 tsp sugar and 80ml (⅓ cup) water and stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper, then cook for 5 mins or until the liquid is absorbed and the beans are warmed through.

Serve up: Meanwhile, put the remaining tomatoes, 2 tsp olive oil and 1 tsp red wine vinegar in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and toss to combine. Divide the Mexi rice and beans among bowls, top with the corn and tomato salsa, then drizzle with the yoghurt. Season with salt and pepper, scatter over the coriander leaves and enjoy!

Make it faster: We've cut the corn a little differently for a bit of fun. Simply stand the corn upright on the cut end so it is stable, then carefully cut from top to bottom to make wedges. If you prefer, slice the kernels off the cob instead and stir-fry over high heat for 2-3 mins until charred.
